name: International Human Rights
new_code: name of the instrument it belongs to (UN Charter, UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR, ECHR, Geneva Conventions, Rome Statute, Constitution of India, Protection of Human Rights Act 1993)
example: Article 4 of the ICCPR, or Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993
example_te: Article 4 — ICCPR lo; Section 12 — Protection of Human Rights Act lo
terms: 'human rights', 'sovereignty', 'covenant', 'derogation', 'non-refoulement', 'due diligence', 'margin of appreciation', 'grave breaches', 'prisoner of war', 'complementarity', 'jus cogens', 'erga omnes', 'ratification', 'reservation', 'treaty body', 'NHRC'

episodes.s: The Nuremberg trial — what human rights mean, the jurisprudential theories, and the evolution from Magna Carta to 1948
episodes.cover: Definition (PHR Act Sec 2(1)(d), Vienna 1993) and the eight characteristics; natural law (Stoics, Aquinas, Locke, Kant), positivism (Bentham, Austin), utilitarianism (Mill, Dworkin's trumps), historical and sociological schools, Marxism, Rawls, Sen and Nussbaum's capabilities, feminist jurisprudence, relativism vs universalism, the Indian tradition; the milestones table from Magna Carta to R2P; Nuremberg and the individual as a subject of international law; jus cogens and erga omnes (Barcelona Traction, Filartiga, Belgium v Senegal)

episodes.s: The Rwandan genocide — the three generations of rights, sovereignty versus human rights, and the United Nations' Charter and organs
episodes.cover: Vasak's three generations with critique; sovereignty — Arts 2(1), 2(4), 2(7); the four stages (not essentially domestic, Chapter VII practice, humanitarian intervention and Nicaragua, R2P 2001-2005 and Libya/Syria); India's position; Charter Preamble, Arts 1(3), 13, 55, 56, 62, 68, 76 and the six organs' roles; promotion vs protection — standard-setting, monitoring, complaints, enforcement, Vienna 1993, SDGs; Akayesu, Namibia, Nicaragua, Bosnia v Serbia

episodes.s: Hansa Mehta and the drafting of the Universal Declaration — its contents, legal status, and the Tehran and Vienna conferences
episodes.cover: The Commission and Drafting Committee (Roosevelt, Cassin, Malik, Chang, Humphrey, Mehta); the 48-0-8 vote; Cassin's portico and the thirty articles table; legal status by four routes (custom, Charter interpretation, treaties, constitutions) and the International Bill of Rights; Proclamation of Tehran 1968 and Vienna Declaration 1993 (universality, indivisibility, women's rights, the High Commissioner); criticisms and the relativist debate; Tehran Hostages, Chandrima Das, Kesavananda, Vishaka

episodes.s: Toonen v Australia — the ICCPR and the ICESCR, their machinery and Optional Protocols, and India's ratification, reservations and case law
episodes.cover: Why two Covenants; ICCPR Arts 1-5 (Art 4 derogation and non-derogable rights), 6-27 article by article, the Human Rights Committee (reports, General Comments, OP1 communications and 'views', OP2 death penalty); ICESCR Art 2(1) progressive realisation, GC 3 minimum core, Arts 6-15, CESCR, OP 2008; India's 1979 declarations, non-ratification of OPs; Jolly George Varghese, Nilabati Behera, PUCL (tapping), Vishaka, Puttaswamy, Navtej Johar, Gramophone Co; Toonen, Lovelace, Broeks

episodes.t: Death Row and the Strasbourg Court
episodes.s: Soering v UK — the European Convention and Court, the Social Charter, and the European Union's Charter and Court of Justice
episodes.cover: Council of Europe; ECHR rights and the limitation-clause structure; Protocols 1-16; Commission and Court to 1998, Protocol 11's permanent Court, admissibility, binding judgments, Committee of Ministers, pilot judgments, interim measures; doctrines — margin of appreciation, proportionality, positive obligations, living instrument, extra-territoriality, absolute Art 3; landmark cases table (Handyside, Dudgeon, Chahal, McCann, Osman, Hirst, Al-Skeini, KlimaSeniorinnen); European Social Charter and collective complaints; EU — general principles, Charter of Fundamental Rights, CJEU, Kadi, Digital Rights Ireland, Schrems, Opinion 2/13, Bosphorus

episodes.s: Velásquez Rodríguez — the Inter-American system, the African Charter and Court, the Arab and ASEAN instruments, and a comparison
episodes.cover: OAS, American Declaration 1948, American Convention 1969 (distinctive articles, Protocol of San Salvador, Belém do Pará), Commission (petitions, precautionary measures, country reports) and Court (contentious, reparations, advisory OC-16/OC-24, compliance); doctrines — due diligence, continuing violation, amnesty invalidity (Barrios Altos), conventionality control (Almonacid), indigenous land (Awas Tingni, Sarayaku), Cotton Field; African Charter 1981 — three generations in one, peoples' rights Arts 19-24, duties Arts 27-29, claw-backs, no derogation, Commission (SERAC, Endorois, Saro-Wiwa), African Court (Mtikila, Ogiek, Konaté), Maputo, Kampala, Malabo; Arab Charter, ASEAN Declaration, why no Asian system; comparison table

episodes.s: Peter Benenson and Amnesty — the UN Commission and Council, OHCHR, treaty bodies, ILO, UNICEF, the NGOs and the ICRC
episodes.cover: Commission on Human Rights 1946-2006 (1235, 1503, special procedures, Sub-Commission); Human Rights Council 2006 (UPR incl. India's reviews, Special Procedures, complaint procedure, commissions of inquiry); Centre for Human Rights to OHCHR (GA 48/141, the High Commissioners); treaty bodies table with India's status; ILO — tripartism, 1998 Declaration, fundamental Conventions, India's ratifications, Committee of Experts, Art 24/26, CFA, Myanmar Art 33; UNICEF's history and rights-based role under CRC Art 45; UNHCR, UNESCO, WHO, UN Women; Amnesty (mandate, methods, India closure 2020), HRW, Indian NGOs, Defenders Declaration; ICRC — origin, mandate under the Conventions, Fundamental Principles, confidentiality, India

episodes.s: Vishaka — CEDAW and the rights of women, the 1959 Declaration and the Convention on the Rights of the Child, and India's law
episodes.cover: From the Charter to CEDAW 1979; Arts 1-16 article by article, Committee, OP 1999 (A.T. v Hungary), GR 19/35; DEVAW, Beijing, Cairo, SCR 1325 and 1820, Istanbul, ILO 190; India's declarations (Arts 5(a), 16(1), 16(2), 29) and the Committee's observations; the cases — Vishaka, Apparel Export, Madhu Kishwar, Githa Hariharan, Anuj Garg, Joseph Shine, Babita Puniya, X v Principal Secretary; the 2005, 2013, 2017 Acts; children — Geneva 1924, the 1959 Declaration's ten principles, CRC 1989 (four principles, the rights grouped, Arts 37-40, Committee, three OPs incl. Sacchi); India's Art 32 declaration, Arts 21A, 23, 24, 39, 45; JJ Act 2015, POCSO 2012, RTE 2009, child labour 2016, child marriage 2006, NCPCR; M.C. Mehta, Bandhua, Lakshmi Kant Pandey, Independent Thought, Salil Bali

episodes.s: Niyamgiri — indigenous peoples, refugees, and the other vulnerable groups in international and Indian law
episodes.cover: ILO 107 (India party) and 169 (Arts 6, 7, 14-16), Martínez Cobo, UNDRIP 2007 (Arts 3, 10, 19, 26, 32), Permanent Forum, Expert Mechanism, FPIC cases; India's position, Fifth and Sixth Schedules, Art 371A, PESA, Forest Rights Act, Land Acquisition Act Sec 41, Samatha, Niyamgiri, Nandini Sundar; refugees — UNHCR, 1951 Convention Art 1A(2), 1C, 1F, rights, Art 31, 33 non-refoulement as custom, OAU and Cartagena, statelessness conventions, IDPs; India's practice — Tibetans, Sri Lankans, Chakmas, Rohingya; Foreigners Act, Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025, CAA 2019, Sec 6A; NHRC v Arunachal, Ktaer Abbas, Salimullah, Sonowal, Gambia v Myanmar; minorities, CRPD and RPwD Act, migrant workers, older persons, LGBTQI+ (NALSA, Supriyo), caste and CERD GR 29, trafficking

episodes.s: Henry Dunant — international humanitarian law: principles, the Geneva Conventions, prisoners of war, civilians, common Article 3, women, and India
episodes.cover: Origin and sources (Lieber, 1864, St Petersburg, Hague 1899/1907, 1949 Conventions, 1977 Protocols, weapons treaties, customary IHL, Martens clause); principles — distinction, military necessity, proportionality, unnecessary suffering, precaution, hors de combat, equal application; the four Conventions' scheme and grave breaches; GC III — Art 4 POW status, Art 5 tribunals, Arts 12-17, labour, discipline, Art 118 repatriation (1971, Abhinandan), Art 126; GC IV — protected persons, Arts 27-34, aliens, occupation Arts 47-78 (Art 49 settlements, Wall opinion), internees; AP I Arts 48-79; common Art 3, Tadić, AP II; women and IHL — GC IV Art 27, AP I 76, Akayesu, Furundžija, Kunarac, Rome Statute, SCR 1820; IHL and human rights (Nuclear Weapons, Wall, Hassan); Geneva Conventions Act 1960 Secs 3-4, 12-14, Monteiro case, India's non-ratification of the Protocols, AFSPA cases

episodes.s: Kulbhushan Jadhav — enforcement through the ICJ, the ad hoc tribunals, the International Criminal Court and the European courts
episodes.cover: ICJ — Statute Arts 34, 36(1)-(2) and India's declaration, 41, 59-60, 65, Charter 94(2); advisory opinions (Reservations, Namibia, Western Sahara, Wall, Chagos, OPT 2024); contentious human-rights cases (Bosnia v Serbia, DRC v Uganda, Diallo, LaGrand, Avena, Belgium v Senegal, Germany v Italy, Jadhav, Gambia v Myanmar, Ukraine v Russia, South Africa v Israel); limits; ICTY/ICTR, Residual Mechanism, hybrid courts, Bangladesh ICT, investigative mechanisms; ICC — Rome Statute Arts 5-8 bis, 11-17, 25, 27, 28, 33, 98, cases (Lubanga, Al Mahdi, Ntaganda, Ongwen), warrants (Al Bashir, Putin, Netanyahu, Duterte), criticisms, India's objections and the absence of domestic genocide law; ECtHR and CJEU as enforcement; universal jurisdiction (Pinochet, Arrest Warrant, Koblenz, Alien Tort Statute)

episodes.s: Chandrima Das — the constitutional mechanism for international human rights in India and the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993
episodes.cover: Preamble, Part III, Part IV incl. Art 51(c), Part IVA, Arts 73, 253, Entry 14, dualism and the incorporation rules (Gramophone Co, Vishaka, Puttaswamy), 44th Amendment and ADM Jabalpur; the Art 21 expansion cases from Maneka to Anuradha Bhasin; PIL — locus standi, epistolary jurisdiction, commissions, continuing mandamus, guidelines, compensation, critique; PHR Act 1993 — Paris Principles, 2006 and 2019 amendments, Secs 2(1)(d), 2(1)(f), 3-11 (NHRC composition, appointment, term), 12 functions, 13-16 powers, 17-18 procedure and steps after inquiry, 19 armed forces, 20 reports, 21-29 SHRCs (A.P. and Telangana), 30-31 Human Rights Courts, 36 limits, 37; the NHRC's work (custodial deaths, Punjab cremations, Gujarat, Manipur), GANHRI accreditation deferral 2023-24; other institutions; assessment — strengths and gaps (CAT, torture law, AFSPA, undertrials, UAPA); Chandrima Das, Nilabati, D.K. Basu, NHRC v Arunachal, Paramjit Kaur, EEVFAM, Puttaswamy
